newsitem.title: FINLAND: EUROPE FOCUS ON EMU MISGUIDED - FINNISH PROFESSOR.
newsitem.headline: EUROPE FOCUS ON EMU MISGUIDED - FINNISH PROFESSOR.

text.p: European leaders' single-minded focus on monetary union is misguided and their energies should be spent on fixing the European Union's unsound institutional structure, a Finnish professor of economics said on Wednesday.

"Europe is shooting itself in the foot by placing so much emphasis on the monetary union," Bengt Holmstrom, professor at M.I.T. Cambridge in the United States, told a seminar according to a summary of his prepared speech.
"The great emphasis placed on EMU makes sense only as a step towards tighter political union," he said.
"If so, this should be clearly stated rather than hidden behind a smoke screen of economic arguments," he added.
Structural problems affecting Europe's economies could not be solved simply by cutting government budgets.
"Politically difficult reforms have to be made," Holmstrom said, listing the labour markets, pensions, taxation and social transfers as areas in need of reform.

"These reforms have been put on hold because of the urgency of EMU," he said. It would be "extremely unfortunate" if political decision-makers on the national level "will try to shift the burden of these decisions onto Brussels," he said.

"The biggest issue overshadowed by EMU is the urgency of political reform. EU's institutional structure is unsound. There is too little transparency, too little accountability and too few checks and balances," Holmstrom said.
Too much responsibility for the EU Commission could lead to more centralised decision-making than would be "either desirable or necessary," he said.
"The future of Europe depends heavily on how it manages to organise cooperation without ending up with an excesive and non-transparent central government," Holmstrom said.
Addressing EMU itself, Holmstrom said too little was known to speak with much confidence. "In all likelihood, the net effects are going to be small in the end," he added.
